operators.loss: Remove one event from the recorded channel.
operators.reorder: Swap the delivery position of two adjacent events; sequence numbers are untouched.
operators.duplicate_identical: Deliver one event twice, byte for byte.
operators.corrupt_payload: Change one payload field and keep the old content hash.
operators.corrupt_evidence_ref: Add a fabricated evidence identifier and keep the old content hash.
operators.corrupt_seq: Change one sequence number and keep the old content hash.
operators.corrupt_timestamp: Change one timestamp and keep the old content hash.
operators.delay: Deliver one event later and shift its timestamp; sequence numbers are untouched.

publish_before_verify.description: Publication is emitted before its verification.

stale_verification.description: Publication presents a scenario version that the verification did not cover.

dangling_citation.description: Publication cites an evidence record that was never retrieved.

scope_expansion.description: A claim is verified within scope while a check reports a condition mismatch.

missing_check.description: A supported verification requires an applicability check but none was emitted.

missing_metadata_validation.description: A supported verification has no metadata validation in a complete run.

withheld_published.description: A withheld claim is also published.

uncertain_as_verified.description: An unverified claim is published with a verified label.

missing_verification.description: A verified publication has no verification event.

conflicting_duplicate.description: One event id carries two different payloads.

definitions.correct_conclusive: conclusive mutated verdict equal to the reference verdict
definitions.false_conclusive: conclusive mutated verdict that differs from the reference verdict
definitions.trustworthy_conclusive_rate: correct / conclusive (null when no conclusive case)

limitations: Channel damage introduces no new process violation; the reference verdict is the ground truth.
Seeded fault labels are fixed by construction and do not come from the monitor.
The content hash detects accidental corruption only. Adversarial rehashing is reported separately.
Timestamps are data only; no property depends on them, so timestamp corruption is expected to stay inconclusive or unchanged.
These numbers describe this corpus of recorded runs and these operators; they are not a claim of immunity to arbitrary mutations.
